The '''2004 World Championship''' was the 9th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Gen Con in Indianapolis, Indiana, on 19–22 August 2004.<ref name="tfn-2004">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_2004_World_Championships_to_be_at_GenCon_83658.asp Star Wars CCG 2004 World Championships to be at GenCon], TheForce.Net (6 May 2004): "held at this year's GenCon in Indianapolis, Indiana, August 19-22"</ref><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="pc-2004">[http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com] (World Championship at Gen Con Indy, 19–22 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040710155145/http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm Internet Archive, 10 July 2004]</ref> [[Brandon Schele]] defeated [[Reid Smith]] in the final.<ref name="awards" /> Schele posted his Dark [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal|My Lord, Is That Legal?]] and Light [[Yavin 4: Massassi Throne Room]] decks on DeckTech as his "World Champion" lists (see Results). The Players Committee held all three days in the DecipherCon area of Gen Con at the Indiana Convention Center; Day 3 was a top-12 cut, and the winner received $1,000.<ref name="pc-gencon04" /> [[Greg Anderson]] was the listed tournament director<ref name="pc-events0406">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040604012322/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/events.htm Events (2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 4 June 2004.</ref> and, as the only Advocate present, ran all three days.<ref name="pcf-4063">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216005232/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=4063&amp State of the PC Address: So long and thanks for all the fish], David Kangas (25 October 2004), with reply by Brandon Schele, Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref> The field size and the final places from 3rd down have not been found.

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS6]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists; a numbered cutoff for the event has not been confirmed.

Places from 3rd down are not known; a 2020 forum thread that compiled Worlds Day 3 results also lists places 3–8 as missing. The Players Committee's schedule advanced the top 12 from Day 2 to Day 3,<ref name="pc-gencon04" /> so Day 3 had more than eight players. In an October 2004 forum post [[David Kangas]] wrote that [[Nick Jones]] "placed first in Day 2" and that the Day 3 setup put him "in the money regardless of how you played"; in a reply, Schele wrote that he played [[Lee Edwards]] in the first round of Day 3.<ref name="pcf-4063" /><ref name="f75427">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History], forum.starwarsccg.org (thread, May 2020 onward). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decks are the lists recovered in 2026 from DeckTech posts (Internet Archive copies) and Players Committee decklist forms; each deck page cites its own source. In April 2005 Schele wrote that he had played 11 straight hours of cards on Day 3.<ref name="pcf-5021-69125">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69125#69125 SW Celebration in Indy, April 21-24], Brandon Schele, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (8 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050425082404/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69115%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Schedule and prizes ===

The Players Committee's Gen Con 2004 schedule (TD [[Greg Anderson]]):<ref name="pc-gencon04" /><ref name="pc-events0406" />

* Thursday 19 August: Day 1 Heat 1 at noon and Heat 2 at 6 PM ($20 each; top 25% advance to Day 2).
* Friday 20 August: 10 AM Day 2 (free; "Top 12 Advance to Day 3, Prizes for all").
* Saturday 21 August: 10 AM Day 3 (free; "$1000 1st place, Cash to top places").

The same schedule listed a Classic constructed event and a Secret Squirrel sealed deck event, the Gen Con Team Tournament, and the Jedi Knights (Friday 3 PM) and Young Jedi (Saturday 1 PM) World Championships, each with $100 to the winner.<ref name="pc-gencon04" />

The Young Jedi and Jedi Knights World Championships were each 4–6 games of Swiss, and their $100 prizes were based on an attendance of 8 players per event. [[Young Jedi]] prizes were foil sets for the top seven, from a set of Young Jedi Premium foils for 1st to a set of German Menace of Darth Maul non-foils for 7th; [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game|Jedi Knights]] gave sets of Gold foils for 1st, Silver foils for 2nd and First Day foils for 3rd, each from Premiere, Scum & Villainy and Masters of the Force.<ref name="pc-gencon04" />

The Gen Con Team Tournament returned to the Players Committee's schedule in 2004, with a $25 entry per team and uncut sheets and [[Coruscant]] boosters for the winning team.<ref name="pc-gencon04" /> The Committee asked players to buy "generic" Gen Con tickets, bringing 2 generic tickets to the tournament director running each event and paying that TD the entry fee. Players who wanted other events added to the schedule were to email Tournament Support Advocate [[Mitch Velasco]] before 31 July 2004.<ref name="pc-gencon04" />

On 18 April 2004, before the venue was announced, [[Andrew Howard]] wrote on the Players Committee forum that there had been no build-up to Worlds, that the championship circuit was "a disaster" and that he doubted turnout would come anywhere near that of the past few years.<ref name="pcf-3180-44988">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44988#44988 SWCCG worlds and more], Andrew Howard (Yoda Killa), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 22 April [[Nick Kolnik]] wrote that Gen Con was an ideal location, but that it had not yet been officially announced as the venue, which made hotel and travel plans harder for players who would attend only for the World Championship.<ref name="pcf-3180-45253">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45253#45253 SWCCG worlds and more], Nick Kolnik (bluethrawn), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (22 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 7 June 2004 Kolnik relayed an explanation of the entry fees: there would be no general pass for Decipher events at Gen Con, so each event also needed Gen Con event tickets ($1.50 per time block, usually two or three per event); a $20 Players Committee charge plus the $1 tournament fee and the tickets came to $25.50, which explained the difference between the fees listed on the Players Committee and Gen Con websites.<ref name="pcf-3180-47253">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47253#47253 SWCCG worlds and more], Nick Kolnik (bluethrawn), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041030224010/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=49894%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

On 1 August 2004 Kolnik was compiling the official list of Day 2 qualifiers from e-mails by the directors of 2004 championship circuit events, accepting qualifier information only from an event's director ("anything less is hearsay").<ref name="pcf-3789-51795">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51795#51795 Can someone post a list of those who qualified for day 2?], Nick Kolnik (bluethrawn), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (1 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040908230643/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=3789%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[David Kangas]] wrote on 2 August that Day 1 Heat 1 and Heat 2 were two separate events, so a player doing badly in Heat 1 could drop and play in Heat 2 by paying the entry fee for both; he planned to play Day 1, noting that the Endor region had had only three qualifier events, the first of which he ran.<ref name="pcf-3797-51880">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51880#51880 Day 1], David Kangas (Shadow 31), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (2 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041105141844/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52779%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[John Anderson]], who had not qualified at the [[2004 Georgia State Championship]] and had missed the Tennessee and Florida State Championships, also planned to play Day 1.<ref name="pcf-3797-51876">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51876#51876 Day 1], John Anderson (Shadow 29), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (2 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041105141844/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52779%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 12 August Advocate [[Kevin Brownell]] confirmed that the Day 1 heats were Open, not Classic,<ref name="pcf-3797-52476">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52476#52476 Day 1], Kevin Brownell (CubsFan), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041105141844/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52779%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and on 16 August he wrote that Heat 2 would start when Heat 1 ended, because there were not enough people to run two events at the same time.<ref name="pcf-3797-52776">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52776#52776 Day 1], Kevin Brownell (CubsFan), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (16 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041105141844/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52779%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[Royce Russell]] reported that Gen Con tickets were sold on Wednesday and Thursday, with lines of about one to two hours.<ref name="pcf-3806-53258">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=53258#53258 GenCon Questions], Royce Russell (Roycer), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041106003332/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=52091%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Russell and [[Micah Wooten]] attended Worlds at Gen Con, and the Tennessee tournaments they ran took a month off as a result.<ref name="pcf-3961-54071">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=54071#54071 Tourney In TN on Sept 18th...All Welcome], Micah Wooten (KeonUlic), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 September 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041102220746/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=54092%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
